result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both emails get every number right and both hit hard on the deadline. A's notes tell the user to confirm the match with the foundation, which second-guesses a fact the user called real and asked not to soften. B never hedges, ties its ending back to the 212 families with 'don't let this January look like last January,' and turns the meal figure into a clear $25 example. Both add a few made-up details (A: children going to bed hungry, shelves getting thinner; B: winter need and shelves emptying fastest). B repeats the donate link in a P.S., which slightly blurs the 'one call to action' item. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both emails get the numbers right, use the deadline and match prominently, and include a strong ask, a subject line and the correct sign-off. B invents more details, such as children going to bed hungry and parents treating the pantry as a last resort. Its notes also tell the user to confirm a match they already said is real. A embellishes less; its only unsupported addition is a general line about winter demand.
